summary: Stringer is a self-hosted RSS reader built with Ruby that provides an alternative to third-party feed aggregation services. It is described as anti-social, meaning it focuses on direct content consumption rather than sharing or community features. As a work-in-progress project distributed under the MIT licence, it allows you to collect and read web feeds on your own infrastructure.
goodFor: This software suits technical users who want a private, self-hosted space for consuming RSS feeds without relying on commercial reader platforms.
watchOut: The project lacks tagged releases and has a modest maintenance score, which may indicate that updates are irregular or installation paths are less polished.
deployNotes: Because it runs on Ruby, you will typically need to provision a persistent database, configure a web and application server stack, and place it behind a reverse proxy for TLS termination.
